text:
support-lead: :rotating_light: Customer escalation — multiple 503/500s from hosted inference (us-west1) starting ~17:12 UTC. Affected customer reports high error rate and tail latency spikes. Support ticket IDs: #4521, #4523. They say requests intermittently return 503 with 'upstream worker unavailable'. Asking for immediate triage and mitigation.

infra-bot: AUTOMATED ALERT: gpu-node-14 (pod inference-runner-14) exited with SIGSEGV (code=139) at 2026-03-15T17:12:22Z, restart_count=6. Recent restarts across pool: [14,15,18]. Pod logs attached to incident. CPU/GPU usage: GPU memory ~98-100% prior to crash. :warning:

ravi: looking at the logs now. early observation: memory climbs steadily for ~12s before the crash. Kernel message shows illegal memory access in aten::native kernel path. snippet:
```
I0115 17:12:22.123 worker.cpp:542] batch_start seq_len=2048 batch_size=16
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered at /workspace/runtime/ops/attention.cu:421
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
Aborted (core dumped)
```
Also seeing "KV prefetch: enabled" in runtime config for this model instance.

anya (sre-oncall): is this correlated to a single model or tenant? customer says they're calling model: redwood/open-13b-q4-prefetch (their app pins variant). Can we confirm model name in crash logs?

ravi: yes crash logs contain model_id: "open-13b-q4-prefetch" and tenant_id: "acct_5X...". Also see request patterns: clients send sequences with prompt tokens ~1800 and max_tokens=512 occasionally — long sequences + large batchsize likely stressing KV cache.

support-lead: customer provided curl repro. Posting sanitized repro here so eng can reproduce quickly:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-13b-q4-prefetch","input":"<2000 token prompt>","max_tokens":512,"batch_size":16}'
```
They noted error rate goes up once concurrent requests > 8.

morgan (eng-ml): we merged a KV prefetch optimization three days ago that changed memory allocation alignment on attention prefetch path. Suspect regression under long sequence lengths. Commit: 7a3b2c9 changed prefetch allocator. Rolling back that change in canary pool reduced crashes in our internal QA.

eng-runtime: immediate mitigation plan:
- route affected tenant to fallback variant (open-13b-noprefetch or open-7b) for now
- reduce default max batchsize for that model in hosted pools to 4
- deploy a transient soft-limit on seq_len to 1024 for that tenant
I can push a routing rule; sample config:
```
routes:
  - tenant: acct_5X...
    model_fallback: open-7b
    overrides:
      max_batch_size: 4
      max_sequence_length: 1024
```
I can apply this in the next 3 min if everyone agrees.

sre-oncall: please apply mitigation. Also increase pod restart backoff so we don't thrash the pool. I'll also temporarily taint nodes with label 'kv-prefetch-regression=true' to prevent scheduling additional instances from the same pool.

infra-bot: I can shift traffic for the tenant to the 'fallback' routing pool and scale up two extra GPU nodes with slightly more VRAM. Will start scale action now.

ravi: after mitigation we should capture a minimized repro and run under valgrind-like memcheck in isolated environment. Until we have a repro, prefer rollback of the prefetch commit for production. Reproduced crash with this test script locally (sanitized):
```
for i in {1..12}; do 
  python stress_client.py --model open-13b-q4-prefetch --prompt tokens=1800 --max_tokens 512 &
done
```
3/12 concurrent clients triggered the segfault for me within ~30s.

morgan: agree. I'll prepare an immediate rollback to commit 4d1e8a2 in canary. Post-rollback, we'll run the nightly regression harness with long-seq tests and stress double concurrency for 2 hours.

support-lead: customer-ops — please inform customer we've applied a fallback and reduced batchsize; request they retry and share results. Keep support ticket open until stable.

customer-ops: pinged customer via email + support channel. They acknowledged and will test in ~10 min. They asked whether this is a billing-impacting mitigation — routing to smaller model will reduce cost and latency, they accept for now.

eng-runtime: quick note: adding a guard to runtime to reject requests with batch_size*seq_len > 20000 for models with prefetch enabled would prevent OOM scenarios. I'll open an RFC ticket and a patch PR to add the guard.

sre-oncall: tracking checklist:
- [x] apply tenant-specific routing overrides
- [x] scale up fallback pool
- [x] set pod restart backoff
- [ ] rollback KV prefetch change in prod canary
- [ ] reproduce with isolated memcheck
- [ ] postmortem + KB entry for 'long-seq prefetch regression'

morgan: created PR #842 to revert commit 7a3b2c9, merging to canary now.

infra-bot: action summary: routing override applied for acct_5X..., fallback model in place, 2 extra nodes scaled, pod backoff increased. Monitoring for 15m window.

support-lead: customer reports reduced 503s after fallback, still watching. We'll keep thread updated. After we stabilize, please prepare a short customer-facing summary and internal postmortem with timeline and root cause analysis.

eng-runtime: noted. I'll follow up with PR for the runtime guard and an integration test to simulate high batch*seq load.

support-lead: thanks everyone. Filing incident for full postmortem — tagging for 72h follow-up. :white_check_mark:
